1.1. A total of 331,086.75 kg of improved seed of sorghum, millet, wheat, sesame, vegetables were distributed in the 9 states. The improved seeds were accompanied by a full climate smart package demonstration plots. An amount of 127,973.75 kg constituting 38.7% of total seed quantities used was secured from previous season Projects’ participant farmers in the 9 states. 1.2. An amount of 127,973.75 kg constituting 38.7% of total seed quantities used was secured from previous season Projects’ participant farmers in the 9 states. The total number of home gardens (Jubrakas) reached 4569 in 56 villages compared to a target of 1250 home gardens for the 2022 1.3. A total of 65.3 tons of nutritive range seeds were collected, 300 km fire lines in Kassala state and 450 Km in Central Darfur were opened, and 26 rangelands reserves were established in the 9 States over a target of 20 reserves. 1.4. A total length of 2,246.0 km of shelterbelts were established in 38 villages in 8 States. Further, 120 community forests were established in 8 States, covering a total area of 38,552 feddan. In addition, 25 tree nurseries were established in 8 States with a total production of 107,933 seedlings. 2.1. The Project completed studies for Rehabilitation of 15 Haffirs and 19 water yards in 4 States (Red Sea, Kassala, West and South Kordofan). Rehabilitation of 28 Haffirs and construction of 24 water yards is progressing to completion in early 2023. Procurement of the First batch of solar systems (120 systems) for Haffirs and extractive pumps is progressing and installation is expected by April 2023. 2.2. No sand dams were established in 2022 due to inflation and shortage of funds allocated for component 2 3.1. the Project trained Project Mangers, cooperatives personnel, extension experts, communities, farmers, women and others in different subjects in the 9 states. A total of 7591 persons, including 3729 women. Communities, farmers and women were trained on issues such as water harvesting techniques, seeds production, land preparation, nursery techniques, food processing, rangelands, seed collection and storage. Project Managers and extension experts from the 9 states were trained on adaptation to climate change, microfinance, cooperatives and monitoring and evaluation.
